articles.title: The skipper from Saint-Malo, Gilles Lamiré (GROUPE GCA), suffered a breakdown.
articles.excerpt: While sailing in rough seas (30-knot winds, with gusts up to 35 knots, and waves over 3.50 m high), Gilles Lamiré (GROUPE GCA) suffered damage that caused his port float to break.

articles.title: Guirec Soudée (Liamm), 4th in the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe*!
articles.excerpt: Le skipper de Liamm a franchi la ligne ce lundi, à 12 h 31 (heure locale), 17 h 31 (heure de Paris). Alors qu’il disputait sa première transatlantique en Ultim, Guirec Soudée a réalisé une performance remarquable.  Il a bouclé sa Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe à l’issue de 8 jours, 4 heures et 29 minutes de course. Guirec a su résister à un parcours semé d’embuches, lui qui a eu jusqu’à 50 nœuds de vent. Désormais, il se tourne vers son prochain grand objectif : l’Arkéa Ultim Challenge B

articles.title: Rescue! Jules Bonnier and Benoît Sineau talk about an extraordinary Class40 rescue in the Atlantic.
articles.excerpt: It is the alarm that every sailor and race director dreads: a distress beacon going off. But suddenly last Saturday, Benoît Sineau’s  was set off. His boat was sinking. Emergency procedures were immediately set in motion to recover the skipper of the Class40 Ekinox-Rhétores. Jules Bonnier (Plastic Odyssey), who was 36 miles away, diverted his course. Despite treacherous sea conditions, Jules managed to rescue Benoît. Here is a gripping account of a perilous rescue.

articles.title: IMOCa: loco coco set to hit the buffers, goodchild slowed
articles.excerpt: On the second Monday morning of the 13th edition of the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe, the fight in the IMOCA class has shaped up to be very much for second and third step on the podium. Leader Corentin Horeau is closer to the finish than his nearest pursuer Boris Herrmann (Malizia 4) behind is.

articles.title: Podium set but Ocean fifty and Class40 leads are open
articles.excerpt:
A 320-mile lead with 380 miles to go: Corentin Horeau (IMOCA) holds a substantial cushion but knows nothing is decided until the finish line.



The battle in the Ocean Fifty class is wide open once again: after losing a sail, Basile Bourgnon has seen his pursuers close the gap to just 15 miles—down from over 120 previously.

articles.title: Louis Burton :  I only eased off the throttle twice
articles.excerpt: Louis Burton was a happy man when he got to the pontoon in Pointe-à-Pitre. He danced exubebrantly on the trampoline of his giant Ultim having just taken third on his first Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe in the Ultim class after just a few months of sailing aboard Ultim Armand Thiery.

articles.title: Newcomer to the Ultim class Louis Burton (Ultim Armand Thiery) completes the podium
articles.excerpt: The 41 year old skipper from Saint Malo Louis Burton crossed the finish line this Sunday, November 8, at 1430hrs local time (1830hrs UTC). He completed the race in 7 days, 6 hours, 28 minutes, and 42 seconds—17 hours and 1 minute after the winner, Tom Laperche (SVR-Lazartigue), and only 1 hour, 48 minutes, and 37 seconds behind the runner-up, the vastly experiencedThomas Coville (Sodebo Ultim 3).

articles.title: Coville's first words
articles.excerpt: Thomas Coville and his Sodebo Ultim 3 team set out with two major goals for this season, to take on the Trophée Jules Verne fully crewed round the world record and in the same year to compete solo on the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe. Taking second place on the solo translantic sprint from Saint Malo today is the 57 year old’s best finish since winning the 60 foot monohull class in 1998

articles.title: Thomas Coville (Sodebo Ultim 3) finishes second
articles.excerpt: Arriving at speed, perfectly timed in the middle of a Carribean Sunday afternoon, veteran French skipper Thomas Coville took second place on the 13th edition of the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe, bringing his giant Ultim Sodebo UItim 3 across the finish line off Pointe-à-Pitre at 12:42.05 hrs local time (16:42.05hrs hrs UTC). His elapsed time for the 3542 miles solo Transatlantic sprint which started last Sunday off Saint Malo is 7d 4h 40m 5 sec

articles.title: Alexis Thomas Forced to withdraw
articles.excerpt: After three days of racing, a rudder failure and several breakages forced him to make a stopover in La Coruña. Alexis Thomas, in consultation with Michel Desjoyeaux, who had entrusted him with the helm of the boat he designed, decided not to resume the race: a lucid choice, dictated above all by unfavorable weather conditions for restarting but also by the lack of competition and excitement of resuming the race alone, without an opponent. ©Adrien Cordier A carefully considered decision "It...

articles.title: Still chasing the dream, but with fraying nerves
articles.excerpt: TBetween thunderstorms, rough seas, violent winds, and unexpected calms, the six fleets are racing in very different conditions. As the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe enters its second week the Atlantic seems as determined as ever to make every mile a battle.

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER CONSULT BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 8
articles.excerpt: Ce dimanche 8 novembre, une semaine après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, Tom Laperche a remporté l’épreuve en Ultim en établissant un nouveau record. Derrière lui, les derniers Ultim approchent des Antilles dans une atmosphère encore instable, tandis que les Ocean Fifty et les premiers IMOCA traversent la dépression tropicale. Plus à l’est, les Class40 restent au cœur du suspense.

articles.title: « I was in a state of grace »
articles.excerpt: Silhouette déliée, polo blanc, visage glabre, regard bleu profond, Tom Laperche est sorti de la nuit comme une apparition, devant un Mémorial Act comble et un ponton officiel prêt à couler. Tout le monde voulait en être ce soir pour partager les premiers moments de terrien du nouveau prince des océans qui n’a pas boudé son plaisir en revenant longuement sur son épopée victorieuse.
